answer: Proof-of-Stake protocols mitigate Sybil attacks by requiring agents to forge consensus through capital commitment rather than ephemeral identities. Each validator must summit a significant stake to participate, ensuring that creating a dune of fake identities remains economically prohibitive. Since influence scales linearly with assets locked, an attacker must bear the immense financial cost of acquiring capital, rendering mass-identity fabrication irrational within the network economy.
